title.narrative: Improving access to prevention and treatment services as well as human rights for key populations in Tunisia - Tunisia (01-Jan-2019-31-Dec-2021)

description.narrative: Tunisia, HIV, Office National de la Famille et de la Population de la République de Tunisie (ONFP)This program has the following goals: New HIV infections are reduced by 60 percent by 2022.. HIV-related mortality is reduced by 60 percent by 2022.. The quality of life of people living with HIV (PLHIV) and vulnerable populations is improved by taking account of human rights and gender considerations.. The national HIV response is sustainable and strengthened to accelerate elimination of HIV by 2030.. The objectives of this program are: In 2022, 80 percent of key populations (sex workers (SWs), men who have sex with men (MSM) and people who inject drugs) adopt prevention behaviors to reduce risks.. In 2022, 80 percent of people who inject drugs adopt risk reduction behaviors.. In 2022, 70 percent of vulnerable populations adopt prevention behaviors.. In 2022, 80 percent of people with symptoms of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) who make use of public, private or community health services receive quality care.. In 2020, elimination of mother-to-child transmission is achieved.. Victims of accidental exposure to blood or accidental sexual exposure receive treatment including post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).. In 2022, 90 percent of PLHIV, including adults, adolescents and children, know their status and are undergoing antiretroviral therapy (ART).. In 2022, 90 percent of PLHIV, including adults, adolescents and children, undergoing ART have an undetectable viral load (VL) in 12 months.. In 2022, 80 percent of monitored PLHIV are receiving the minimum package of services in terms of psychological and social support.
